diagnostics.message: :resource.google_compute_project_default_network_tier.default_network_tier sets the project-level default network tier via compute.projects.setDefaultNetworkTier, which requires the Compute Engine API to be enabled in the project. Nothing in the graph orders it after :resource.google_project_service.project_services (its only attribute inputs are var.default_network_tier and local.project.project_id, which is just project creation). Its sibling in main.tf, google_compute_project_metadata_item.default, carries exactly this guard (\"Only usable if compute API has been enabled\"), so this resource can fail with an API-not-enabled error on a first apply that enables compute.googleapis.com in the same run. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project to a Shared VPC host, which requires compute.googleapis.com to be enabled in the service project first. Its depends_on only covers the VPC-SC perimeter resources; there is no path to :resource.google_project_service.project_services (the other shared-VPC resources in the same file — google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host explicitly, and service_projects transitively via its host_project dependency — are both ordered after the API enablement). First-apply runs that enable compute in the same plan can fail here. Add google_project_service.project_services to the depends_on list.

:resource.google_essential_contacts_contact.contact creates Essential Contacts via the essentialcontacts.googleapis.com API, which is not enabled by default on a new project and must be enabled through :resource.google_project_service.project_services (var.services) before contact creation succeeds. The graph only records its depends_on on the IAM binding/member resources, and the contact's `parent` is a plain string, so no ordering with the API enablement is inferred; creating the contact in the same apply that enables essentialcontacts.googleapis.com can fail with a 403 "API has not been used/enabled" error. Add google_project_service.project_services to depends_on.
